 Diwali 2026 will be celebrated in November, bringing together five days of prayers, family traditions and festivities. Also known as Deepawali, the festival is marked by the worship of Goddess Lakshmi, the lighting of diyas, the exchange of sweets and rituals that celebrate prosperity and the victory of good over evil.
 The five main observances begin with Dhanteras and conclude with Bhai Dooj. In between, families celebrate Narak Chaturdashi, Diwali and Govardhan Puja, with each day carrying a distinct religious and cultural significance. In 2026, the main Diwali celebrations are scheduled around November 8. Festival dates can vary by region and local Panchang, particularly when tithis overlap, so devotees should check the timings followed in their city.

 Diwali 2026: Five-Day Festival Calendar 
 The five major observances in 2026 will fall between November 6 and November 11. Unlike a typical year, they will not take place on five consecutive dates because of the way the lunar tithis fall. 
 Festival Date and Time 
 Govatsa Dwadashi (Vasu Baras) Thursday, November 5, 2026 
 Dhanteras, Dhanvantari Trayodashi, Yama Deepam Friday, November 6, 2026 
 Kali Chaudas, Hanuman Puja Saturday, November 7, 2026 
 Narak Chaturdashi, Diwali, Lakshmi Puja, Kali Puja Sunday, November 8, 2026 
 Diwali Snan, Diwali Devpuja Monday, November 9, 2026 
 Govardhan Puja, Annakut, Bali Pratipada, Gujarati New Year Tuesday, November 10, 2026 
 Bhai Dooj, Bhau Beej, Chitragupta Puja Wednesday, November 11, 2026 
 1. Dhanteras 2026: November 6 
 Dhanteras, also known as Dhantrayodashi, marks the beginning of the main five-day Diwali festivities. The occasion is associated with Goddess Lakshmi, Lord Dhanvantari and Lord Kuber, and is considered auspicious for seeking wealth, good health and prosperity.
 Many families buy gold, silver, utensils and other household items on this day. Homes and shops are cleaned and decorated, while devotees perform Dhanteras Puja in the evening. Lighting a diya in the name of Yama, known as Yama Deepam, is another important tradition.

 2. Kali Chaudas 2026: November 7

 Kali Chaudas is observed on the eve of the main Diwali celebrations in parts of western India, particularly Gujarat. The day is associated with Goddess Kali and is observed through prayers seeking protection from negative forces and evil.
 Devotees also worship Lord Hanuman in some regions. Rituals vary across communities, and the observance is sometimes associated with Narak Chaturdashi, although the two can fall on different dates depending on local traditions and Panchang calculations.

 3. Narak Chaturdashi and Diwali 2026: November 8 
 November 8 will be the main Diwali day in 2026. It will also be observed as Narak Chaturdashi in the New Delhi calendar. Narak Chaturdashi, popularly known as Choti Diwali, is associated with the victory of Lord Krishna over the demon Narakasura. The occasion symbolises the triumph of good over evil. Many households observe an early morning ritual bath, known as Abhyang Snan, followed by prayers and other traditional customs.
 In the evening, families celebrate Diwali by lighting earthen lamps, decorating their homes, exchanging sweets and performing Lakshmi-Ganesh Puja.
 Diwali 2026 Lakshmi Puja Muhurat 
 Lakshmi Puja is traditionally performed during Pradosh Kaal, the period after sunset when Amavasya tithi prevails. For New Delhi, the Lakshmi Puja muhurat on November 8 is listed as 5:54 pm to 7:50 pm. The Amavasya tithi is expected to begin at 11:27 am on November 8 and end at 12:31 pm on November 9.
 These timings are location-specific, and devotees should check their local Panchang before performing the rituals.
 4. Govardhan Puja 2026: November 10 
 Govardhan Puja, also known as Annakut, will be celebrated on Tuesday, November 10. The festival commemorates the day Lord Krishna lifted Govardhan Hill to protect the people of Vrindavan from torrential rain sent by Lord Indra.
 Devotees prepare a variety of food offerings, arrange them as Annakut and offer prayers to Lord Krishna. The occasion also highlights gratitude towards nature, agriculture and cattle. Bali Pratipada and the Gujarati New Year are also observed around this time in several communities.
 5. Bhai Dooj 2026: November 11 
 Bhai Dooj, also known as Bhaiya Dooj, Bhau Beej and Yama Dwitiya, will be celebrated on Wednesday, November 11. The festival honours the bond between brothers and sisters. Sisters perform the traditional tilak ceremony and pray for their brothers' health, happiness and long life. Brothers offer gifts and reaffirm their love and support.
 The occasion is also associated with the legend of Yamraj and his sister Yamuna. Chitragupta Puja is observed by some communities on the same day.
 Why do Diwali dates change every year? 
 Diwali is observed on Amavasya, or the new moon day, of the Hindu lunar month of Kartik in many traditions. Since the Hindu calendar follows lunar movements, the festival falls on different dates in the Gregorian calendar each year.
 The dates of individual observances are determined by the tithi relevant to each ritual. For instance, Lakshmi Puja is performed when Amavasya prevails during Pradosh Kaal, while other festivals follow their own sunrise or tithi-based rules. This also explains why the five main Diwali observances in 2026 will stretch across six calendar dates, rather than falling on five consecutive days.
 Sources and date reference: The 2026 festival schedule and New Delhi puja timings have been cross-checked against published Panchang and festival calendars. Regional observances may differ.
